chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Nu'aym ibn Ibrahim from 'Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basri said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man freed his Umm al-Walad (concubine mother of his child) and made her manumission her dowry, then he divorced her before consummating the marriage with her. He said: 'He offers her that she seeks reduction (of her value) in half of her price; if she refuses, then half of her is slave and half is free.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Umm al-Walad: A female slave who bears a child to her master, entitling her to manumission upon the master's death or specific conditions.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an Umm al-Walad whose manumission is her dowry if divorced before consummation?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial settlement for an Umm al-Walad whose manumission was pledged as her dowry, ruling that if divorced before consummation, she may choose to accept half her value as a reduction to secure full freedom. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of offering the enslaved woman agency in her emancipation process, balancing the master's financial rights with her status. The scenario underscores the intersection of marriage contracts, manumission deeds, and divorce settlements in classical Islamic jurisprudence.
